_doc: Single source of truth for SDV 1.6 image specs. frame_w/frame_h in game pixels. Sheets are row-major: frame index = row*cols + col. gen_w/gen_h = SDXL-bucket generation size per frame. 'vanilla_ref' names the vanilla sheet the layout was measured from (python vanilla.py specs re-checks every rule against the unpacked game).

portrait.prompt: portrait of {subject}, head and shoulders, facing viewer, {expression} expression, flat background
portrait.notes: Dialogue $0-$5 / $h $s $u $l $a map to frames 0-5. Extra rows allowed (index 6+, used via $N). Width must stay 128.

vanilla_ref.note: 128 wide, height a multiple of 64 (vanilla sheets hold more than the 6 standard frames: Abigail is 10)

portrait_hd.desc: Portraiture / HD portrait sheet (same layout, larger frames)
portrait_hd.prompt: portrait of {subject}, head and shoulders, facing viewer, {expression} expression, flat background
portrait_hd.notes: frame size may be 128, 256 or 512 (pass --frame). Portraiture infers frame size from sheet width / 2.

character_sprite.prompt: full body pixel art sprite of {subject}, {direction} view, walking pose, chibi proportions, plain white background
character_sprite.notes: Rows: 0 down, 1 right, 2 up, 3 left. Vanilla NPC sheets add more rows for animations (indices referenced from schedules/Data/animationDescriptions). Feet sit on the bottom pixel row. Children/small NPCs may use 16x16 or 16x24 frames — pass --frame.

vanilla_ref.note: 64 wide, height a multiple of 32 (the 4 walking rows come first; vanilla adds animation rows below)

object_icon.desc: Object / item icon (Data/Objects, weapons, tools icons)
object_icon.prompt: single {subject} item icon, pixel art game item, centered, plain white background
object_icon.notes: Custom item sheets may be any width that is a multiple of 16; SpriteIndex counts left-to-right, top-to-bottom.

vanilla_ref.note: 384 wide = 24 columns of 16x16; SpriteIndex counts left to right, top to bottom

big_craftable.prompt: {subject}, pixel art game machine, front view, plain white background
big_craftable.notes: Machines with working animation use consecutive indices (e.g. idle + working frames).

crop.prompt: {subject} plant, growth stage {stage}, pixel art crop in soil, side view, plain white background
crop.notes: One 128x32 cell per crop (the vanilla sheet holds two cells per 256 px row; Data/Crops SpriteIndex counts cells). A crop uses len(DaysInPhase)+2 columns: one per growth phase, then the harvestable sprite, then one more (the harvested/regrow or tint frame); columns after that stay empty. Measured on parsnip (4 phases -> 6 columns) and cauliflower (5 phases -> 7 columns).

vanilla_ref.note: 256 wide = two crop cells of 128x32 per row; SpriteIndex counts 128x32 cells

fruit_tree.prompt: {subject} fruit tree, {stage}, pixel art, plain white background
fruit_tree.notes: 432x80 per tree (9 frames of 48x80); Data/FruitTrees TextureSpriteRow counts 80 px rows (vanilla sheet: 9 trees, 432x720). Frame order inside a row is not documented in the game files: copy a vanilla row as the guide before drawing.

vanilla_ref.note: 432 wide = 9 frames of 48x80; one tree per 80 px row (TextureSpriteRow)

furniture.prompt: {subject}, pixel art furniture, three-quarter top-down view, plain white background
furniture.notes: Pass --frame WxH as tilesWide*16 x tilesHigh*16 (e.g. 32x32 for a 2x2 table). Rotatable furniture needs one frame per rotation laid out left to right.

hat.prompt: {subject} hat, {direction} view, pixel art, plain white background
hat.notes: Each hat is a 20x80 strip (4 directions of 20x20 stacked); the vanilla sheet lays hats out 12 per row (240x880). Direction order inside the strip was not measured: copy a vanilla hat as the guide.

vanilla_ref.note: grid of 20 px columns; each hat is a 20x80 strip (4 directions of 20x20 stacked)

shirt.prompt: {subject} shirt torso, {direction} view, pixel art, plain white background
shirt.notes: Dyeable shirts have a matching mask 128px to the right on the vanilla sheet. For anything beyond vanilla shirts use Fashion Sense.

vanilla_ref.note: 256 wide: 128 px of shirts (8 px wide, 4 directions of 8x8 stacked) plus the dye mask 128 px to the right

fs_hair.prompt: {subject} hairstyle only, {direction} view, pixel art, no face, plain white background
fs_hair.notes: Match HairSize and StartingPosition in hair.json to the layout you produce.

fs_accessory.prompt: {subject} accessory, {direction} view, pixel art, plain white background
fs_accessory.notes: Set AccessorySize in accessory.json to frame size.

alt_texture.prompt: {subject} variant {n}, pixel art, plain white background
alt_texture.notes: frame = TextureWidth x TextureHeight of the target, rows = Variations (stacked vertically). Frame size and variation layout follow the target asset's own vanilla frame size.

tilesheet.prompt: seamless {subject} tile texture, top-down view, pixel art game tileset
tilesheet.notes: Generate per-tile or per-object chunk; seamless ground tiles benefit from img2img on a tiled placeholder. Keep tilesheet dimensions fixed once maps reference it (tile indices depend on width).

building.prompt: {subject} farm building exterior, pixel art, three-quarter top-down view, plain white background
building.notes: Width = Size.X*16. Height = Size.Y*16 + roof overhang. Pass --frame WxH.

vanilla_ref.note: width = Size.X x 16 (Barn: 7 x 16 = 112); height = Size.Y x 16 plus the roof overhang
